comment: Delays on silicon as factors of the slow corner, by routing switch class and cell type, fitted from ring oscillators measured on a chip (SKALP examples/delay_calibration).

measured.device: LFCPNX-100-9 (Versa board, one chip), room temperature, nominal core supply
measured.method: 33 ring oscillators in three builds of ring probes (SKALP examples/delay_calibration/gen_probe.py and two earlier probes with the same rings), each measured on the chip against the 125 MHz board clock over two loads, and simulated with the build's routed delays: latch rings placed freely and pinned to the centre and corners, a long-wire ring between opposite corners, and rings through CCU2 carry chains, MULT18X18, DPR16X4 and the clock network. One factor per group (examples/delay_calibration/groups_nexus.json), fitted by non-negative least squares on relative period error with examples/delay_calibration/fit_calibration.py.
measured.results: rings match within 1.45% rms (worst +3.91%). Standard errors: stage 0.057, span0 0.27, span1 0.13, span2 0.15, span6 0.012, carry 0.013, mult 0.008, dram 0.06, clocked 0.012. A design of about 50 thousand cells simulates 1.3% faster than its measured throughput with a 1.0185 derate (the whole-die slowdown measured while it runs).
measured.notes: Ring placement did not matter, nor dense idle logic around a ring, nor heat. Some latch rings come up in a faster mode on some loads (12-28%); those loads were left out. The previous file (fitted outside SKALP's calibrated path) was 10% slow on the carry and RAM rings.
